analysis.file_name: BofA_China Viewpoint 2027 Year Ahead- Domestic demand still waiting for a spark_20261123.pdf
analysis.title: China Viewpoint 2027 Year Ahead: Domestic demand still waiting for a spark
key_insights: BofA raises 2026 China GDP growth forecast to 4.6% yoy from 4.5%, mainly a mark-to-market for the first three quarters. 4Q26 is forecast at about 4.7% yoy, within the 4.5% to 5.0% government target.
Below-consensus 2027 and 2028 GDP forecasts are unchanged at 4.2% and 4.0%. Policy stimulus is expected to fade in early 2027, which puts next year's growth target in test.
Recent measures include RMB800bn via the policy financing tool in Sep and Oct and RMB550bn of unused local-government debt quotas activated. October data showed no visible improvement yet.

Domestic demand stays weak. Retail sales growth should improve on base effects as trade-in subsidies roll off (2.1% in 2027F vs 1.2% in 2026F), but underlying household demand stays subdued without broader consumption support including services.

Investment: FAI is forecast to rebound to 2.5% in 2027 from -7.9% in 2026 on a very low base. Manufacturing capacity utilization is at a record low and EU-China trade tensions are broadening, so a manufacturing investment rebound is unlikely.

Property remains a drag. The August 28 property sales policy shifting away from presales raises concerns of a further double-digit slowdown in property investment over two years, and falling land sales revenue constrains local governments.

Exports remain a relative bright spot but slow to a high-single-digit pace in 2027 (9.6% forecast) from more than 20% in 2026 (24.1%). Drivers are hyperscaler capex normalization, trade frictions such as on EVs, and a higher base from 2Q.

CPI forecasts are 0.9%, 0.7% and 1.0% for 2026, 2027 and 2028, with PPI at 1.2% in 2027. Weak demand and China's refined-oil price smoothing limit oil pass-through, and BofA commodity strategists see Brent averaging $80/bbl in 2027.

Policy in 2027 is targeted, not broad. No policy rate or RRR cuts are expected unless exports deteriorate materially, and the deficit stays at 4.0%. Special treasury bonds stay at RMB1.3tn and the LGSB quota edges up to RMB4.5tn from RMB4.4tn.

The RMB2tn annual special refinancing bond program ends this year, removing a source of fiscal relief for local governments. No further special bond issuance for bank recapitalization is expected, and PSL is expected to expand beyond this year's RMB800bn.

The shift from the 7-day to the overnight reverse repo rate is seen as a framework change, not a signal of rate cuts. Weak loan growth, with household loans contracting, means modest cuts would not lift credit demand.

Key downside risk is policy inaction. A sharper export slowdown could trigger stronger easing, but an insufficient response would leave growth exposed. Other risks are weaker AI capex, less effective fiscal support and trade frictions.
BofA forecasts USD/CNY at 6.60 at end-2026, 6.45 at end-2027 and 6.30 at end-2028.

sector_views.rationale: The new presales policy could constrain developer cash flow and push property investment down by a double-digit pace over two years.
Exports remain a relative bright spot but growth slows to high-single digits as hyperscaler capex normalizes and the base rises.

tension_points.bull_case: A sharper export slowdown could prompt more forceful easing and a clearer pivot to domestic demand, partially offsetting the shock.
tension_points.bear_case: Policy support stays incremental even as external demand weakens, leaving growth increasingly exposed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A more pronounced export slowdown than BofA expects, or growth deteriorating materially with capital-market stress, would shift BofA toward expecting rate or RRR cuts and a larger deficit.

theme_stances.key_argument: Without more substantial consumption support, underlying household demand should remain subdued despite base-effect gains in retail sales.
theme_stances.evidence: Without more substantial consumption support, underlying household demand should remain subdued

theme_stances.key_argument: Policy support in 2027 is expected to be targeted rather than broad-based, with no rate or RRR cuts.
theme_stances.evidence: A policy cushion, not a stimulus rescue
